signals.title: HeRE: A Novel Benchmark for Hebrew Relation Extraction via LLM-Guided Denoising of Knowledge Graph Alignments
signals.summary: While LLMs demonstrate strong capabilities in English Relation Extraction (RE) tasks, a significant gap remains in assessing their RE performance in low-resource languages, due to a lack of standardized benchmarks. Creating native, language-specific annotated RE benchmarks is expensive and requires human expertise, while relying on translation yields suboptimal, inaccurate datasets that introduce English-centric biases.
signals.implication: Update constitutional clauses and compliance mappings for community operators. Monitor adoption pressure and revise formation cadence for tool onboarding. High relevance to C2A2 operations; include in next leadership brief.
signals.long_summary: The development of benchmarks for Relation Extraction (RE) in low-resource languages, particularly Hebrew, is highlighted as a critical need due to the proven capabilities of large language models (LLMs) in English tasks. The absence of standardized benchmarks hampers the evaluation of LLM performance in these languages, as creating native annotated datasets is costly and requires human involvement. Furthermore, utilizing translated datasets can lead to inaccuracies and biases rooted in English, undermining the effectiveness of the models. This discourse emphasizes the importance of establishing reliable evaluation frameworks for low-resource languages to ensure fair and accurate AI application across diverse languages. Understanding these challenges is essential for a community aiming to keep pace with AI developments, especially in ensuring equitable language representation in AI technologies.

signals.title: RealCLI: Toward a Unified Evaluation of Human-Agent Collaboration for CLI Agents
signals.summary: Command-line interface (CLI) agents increasingly execute longer-horizon tasks, yet existing benchmarks either assume that user instructions remain fixed throughout execution or evaluate task outcomes without capturing runtime collaboration quality. In this paper, we present REALCLI, a paired benchmark that unifies the evaluation of task execution and human-agent collaboration quality on realistic CLI tasks.
signals.implication: Reassess role boundaries and human override for community deployments. High relevance to C2A2 operations; include in next leadership brief.
signals.long_summary: REALCLI is a new benchmark presented to address the shortcomings of current evaluations of command-line interface (CLI) agents, which typically either presume that user instructions do not change during execution or focus solely on the outcomes of tasks without assessing the quality of collaboration between humans and agents during execution. This benchmark aims to unify how both task execution and collaborative interaction quality are evaluated in realistic CLI scenarios. By focusing on longer-horizon tasks where collaboration variability is crucial, REALCLI supports a more comprehensive understanding of human-agent partnerships. This advancement is significant for the community, as it provides a clearer framework for improving and assessing the effectiveness of AI agents in collaborative settings, ultimately enhancing user experience and task success in real-world applications.

signals.title: CF-NODE: Counterfactual Spatial Node Intervention for Test-Time Adaptation Under Domain Shift, Evaluated Across Five Diabetic Retinopathy Datasets
signals.summary: Automated fundus-based diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading can substantially expand screening capacity, but source-trained models degrade sharply across different cameras, clinics, and patient populations. Existing test-time adaptation methods depend on entropy minimization or target information accumulated from image batches and streams.
signals.implication: High relevance to C2A2 operations; include in next leadership brief.
signals.long_summary: The paper discusses a method called CF-NODE aimed at improving the testing adaptability of automated diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading across varying conditions such as different cameras, clinics, and patient demographics. It highlights that while automated grading can enhance screening capabilities, models trained on specific sources tend to perform poorly when faced with new environments. Current adaptation methods often rely on techniques like entropy minimization or the collection of target information from image batches, which may not address all the challenges encountered during testing. By presenting this research, it underscores the importance of developing robust models that can maintain performance in diverse settings. Understanding such developments is crucial for a community engaged in AI, as they indicate directions for improving AI applications in healthcare.

signals.title: Inductive Learning of Concept Embeddings from Cross-Linguistic Colexification Patterns with Textual Attributes
signals.summary: The advent of distributional semantics as a framework for computational semantics marked a paradigm shift in the nature of representations, by which meanings are represented as dense vectors commonly known as word embeddings. Computational approaches to historical or typological language comparison, on the other hand, still mostly rely on discrete representations, while the potential of embedding-based methods remains largely untapped in this context.
signals.implication: Track for context; no immediate governance action required.
signals.long_summary: The paper discusses how the rise of distributional semantics has transformed meaning representations into dense vectors known as word embeddings, suggesting a significant shift in computational semantics. However, it points out that traditional methods for historical or typological language comparison continue to predominantly use discrete representations, highlighting an underutilized opportunity for embedding-based approaches in this area. This gap presents potential for advancement in understanding language relations and meanings through methods that can incorporate the insights provided by word embeddings. This matters for our community as it emphasizes the need to explore innovative methodologies in AI that could enhance our comprehension of language dynamics and their applications.

signals.title: Broad and Efficient PII Detection with Unified Labels
signals.summary: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) detection models must efficiently find identifiers across diverse contexts while maintaining a low false-positive rate (FPR) on high-volume traffic. Recent detectors increasingly rely on complex architectures that raise deployment cost, yet many are fine-tuned on only a few synthetic datasets that limit their coverage.
signals.implication: Track for context; no immediate governance action required.
signals.long_summary: The abstract discusses challenges in Personally Identifiable Information (PII) detection models, emphasizing the necessity for these models to effectively identify PII across varied contexts while keeping the false-positive rate low, especially in high-traffic situations. It points out that many recent PII detectors utilize complex architectures that can increase deployment costs. Furthermore, these models are often fine-tuned using only a limited number of synthetic datasets, which may restrict their ability to cover a broader range of scenarios. Understanding these challenges is crucial for the community to ensure that PII detection technologies remain efficient and widely applicable in everyday use.

signals.title: Mitigating Demographic Disparities in Explanation-Human Alignment via Rationale Regularization
signals.summary: We study explanation fairness in hate speech detection. High classification performance does not always mean that a model produces equally plausible explanations for different demographic groups.
signals.implication: Track for context; no immediate governance action required.
signals.long_summary: The study examines the fairness of explanations generated by models used in hate speech detection, highlighting that while a model may achieve high classification performance, it does not guarantee that the explanations provided are equally plausible across different demographic groups. This suggests a potential disparity where certain groups may receive less reliable or comprehensible explanations than others. Understanding and addressing these issues is crucial for ensuring that AI systems are equitable and transparent. This matters for a community keeping up with AI as it underscores the importance of fairness in AI explanations, which is essential for broader acceptance and responsible deployment of AI technologies.

signals.title: alkhder at AlexandriaX-2026: Context-Aware English-to-Dialectal Arabic Dialogue Translation with QLoRA-Fine-Tuned NileChat-3B
signals.summary: This paper describes team Alkhder's submission to Subtask 1 of the AlexandriaX-2026 shared task, which asks systems to translate English dialogue turns into thirteen Arabic dialects. We fine-tune NileChat-3B-Base with QLoRA on the Alexandria parallel dialogue corpus, training one set of adapter weights for all dialects.
signals.implication: Track for context; no immediate governance action required.
signals.long_summary: Team Alkhder has submitted a paper detailing their approach to Subtask 1 of the AlexandriaX-2026 shared task, which involves translating English dialogue into thirteen Arabic dialects. They utilized the NileChat-3B-Base model fine-tuned with QLoRA on the Alexandria parallel dialogue corpus. Their method focuses on creating a single set of adapter weights that can effectively translate across all the specified dialects. This work demonstrates advancements in multilingual dialogue translation capabilities. Keeping up with such innovations is crucial for the community to understand the evolving dynamics of language processing in AI.

signals.title: From Parallels to Divergence: Language Models' Learning of Action Nominal Constructions
signals.summary: Action nominal constructions (ANCs) express events in nominal form, with their argument marking following patterns found in clauses or ordinary noun phrases. In this paper, we investigate how different grammatical configurations affect language models' learning of ANCs and related constructions, and how these learning preferences compare with typological distributions in natural languages.
signals.implication: Track for context; no immediate governance action required.
signals.long_summary: This study examines the impact of various grammatical configurations on how language models learn action nominal constructions (ANCs), which represent events in a nominal format. It also explores how the learning preferences of these models relate to the typological distributions observed in natural languages. By dissecting these learning patterns, the research highlights the distinctions between the ways language models acquire knowledge of ANCs compared to human language typology. Understanding these differences is crucial for improving AI's grasp of nuanced linguistic forms, which can enhance the development of more sophisticated language processing technologies. This matters for our community as it sheds light on the intricacies of language model training, fostering a deeper comprehension of their capabilities and limitations in natural language understanding.

signals.title: Diagnosing GNN Failure Modes with Layer-Wise Probe Entropy
signals.summary: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are typically evaluated only at their final layer, obscuring how task-relevant information evolves during message passing. We introduce a post-hoc diagnostic that freezes a trained GNN, fits an independent linear probe to each layer, and tracks probe accuracy alongside normalized predictive entropy.
signals.implication: Track for context; no immediate governance action required.
signals.long_summary: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are usually assessed only at the final layer, making it difficult to understand the progression of task-relevant information throughout the message passing process. This work presents a new diagnostic technique that involves freezing a trained GNN and fitting an independent linear probe to each layer. The method monitors the accuracy of the probes and measures normalized predictive entropy, allowing for a comprehensive analysis of how information flows and evolves in GNNs. This approach can help identify where failures occur within the network, providing deeper insights into its functionality and potential areas for improvement. Understanding these dynamics is crucial for the community to enhance the reliability and effectiveness of GNN applications in various domains.

signals.title: Noise-Robust Forced Alignment for Spontaneous Speech
signals.summary: We show that forced aligners degrade on spontaneous, noisy real-world speech, and that fillers, laughter, and disfluencies corrupt word boundaries, impacting many downstream applications. We revisit the classical GMM-HMM aligner with upsampled WavLM features instead of MFCCs, explicit phone units for fillers and non-lexical vocal events trained on verbatim-annotated spontaneous speech, and a discriminative projection fitted on clean and noise-corrupted feature pairs to improve robustness.
signals.implication: Track for context; no immediate governance action required.
signals.long_summary: Forced alignment tools currently struggle with spontaneous and noisy real-world speech due to complications such as fillers, laughter, and disfluencies, which disrupt accurate word boundary detection and affect downstream applications. The authors propose enhancements to the classical GMM-HMM aligner by using upsampled WavLM features in place of traditional MFCCs. They also incorporate explicit phone units for fillers and non-lexical vocal events, trained on verbatim annotated spontaneous speech. Additionally, a discriminative projection is employed, developed using both clean and noise-corrupted feature pairs, to bolster the robustness of the alignment process. This research is significant for the community as it addresses the challenges of accurately processing informal speech in various applications, underlining the need for more resilient AI tools in real-world contexts.
